extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and applicants (particularly those seeking or examining patent term extensions in Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examination criteria governing applications to register patent term extension in Korea, including requirements for approvals, identicalness of composition/use, applicant eligibility, amendment treatment, procedural notices, and extensions for registration delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of approval under relevant Acts for practicing patented invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A patented invention subject to an application to register patent term extension needs to be approved under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, etc. for the practicing of the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check whether the approval needed under relevant provisions to manufacture the drug has been obtained; examiners may not additionally examine necessity of approval unless special conditions exist (e.g., third-party objection). If unsure, examiner may conduct additional examination (request opinion from relevant organizations). If approval is deemed not required based on examination results, examiner shall notify the ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness of compositions between patented substance and approved substance
rubrics_metrics.description: The approved substance shall have the same composition as the substance recited in claims in an application to register patent term extension (where the claimed invention is a substance) or as the matter manufactured by the method described in claims (where the claimed invention is a use of a substance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) For a substance invention, an examiner shall compare the concerned substance and the approved substance. (ii) For a manufacturing-method invention, an examiner shall compare the substance manufactured by the disclosed method with the approved substance; the manufacturing methods need not be compared. Where compositions are not identical, deem it a ground for rejection under Article 91(1) of the Patent Act and notify applicant of the ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness of use for use inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patented subject matter is a use invention, the use of the approved substance must be the same as the use disclosed in the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the use of the approved substance is not the same as the claimed use, the patent term shall not be extended even if compositions are identical. However, when the use of the patented substance includes the use of the approved substance, it shall be deemed that the uses are the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of intermediates, catalysts, and manufacturing devices from extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights regarding a manufacturing device for a final product and a catalyst used for manufacturing an intermediate and final product shall not be subject to extension of the patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts governing safety (e.g., Pharmaceutical Affairs Act) govern manufacture/sale of final products, not intermediates. An intermediate does not need approval. Applications to register extension for intermediates, catalysts, or manufacturing devices based on approval of a final product should be rejected under Article 91(1)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant eligibility — applicant must be the patentee at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who files an application to register patent term extension shall be the patentee at the time of filing the application for registration of extension; even a person who has an exclusive or non-exclusive license cannot be the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where irregularities exist (e.g., person not eligible filed the application), examiner shall notify grounds for rejection rather than making an amendment request or returning the application. If a patentee or licensee who was not registered at time of filing obtains approval later, it falls under grounds for rejection under Article 91(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership requirement — all co-owners must file
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent right is jointly owned, an application to register an extension of the term of the patent right shall be filed by all the co-owners of the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only some co-owners file, it falls under grounds for rejection under Article 91(1)(5) of the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum extension limited to period invention could not be practiced; calendar calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The term for which an extension is applied shall not exceed the period during which the patented invention could not have been practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term does not need to exactly match the period; if the applied-for extension term has not elapsed even if incorrectly calculated, an examiner shall acknowledge the term rather than notifying ground for rejection. Calculation of the term for which an extension is applied shall be conducted based on calendar. (Note: if approval date is before the date of registration for establishment of patent right, it is ground for rejection under Article 91(3).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of grounds for rejection — content and argument period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where examiner intends to reject an application to register patent term extension, the examiner shall notify the applicant of the ground for rejection and give opportunity to submit a written argument within a designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall indicate relevant provisions or grounds for rejection precisely and concisely. At delivery, notify applicant that written argument shall be submitted within two months. The period for submission can be extended: allowed one additional month each time, up to three times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of written arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can submit written arguments in response to a notice of grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written argument shall be submitted within the designated period. Where an argument is submitted, the examiner shall determine whether the ground for rejection really exists while considering the applicant’s claims in the written argument. Even if an argument is submitted after the period has elapsed or before notification, examiner shall take the argument into consideration rather than returning it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amendments — permissible timing and re-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit an amendment in response to grounds for rejection, subject to timing and scope restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment can be presented before delivering a copy of decision to grant registration of extension. After notice of grounds for rejection, an applicant can submit an amendment only within the period for submission of argument. Where an amendment is submitted, the examiner shall re-examine the application reflecting the amended matters, as long as the amendment is refused to be entered. When amendment is recognized legitimate, examiner shall examine the amended application while deeming that the application was submitted at the time of filing the initial application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters eligible for amendment under Article 90(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters eligible for amendment in an application for registration of extension under Article 90(6) include specific items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible items include: ① an indication of claims for registration of extension, ② the period for extension request, ③ the content of approval, etc. under Article 89 of the Patent Act, ④ the ground for extension specified in Ordinance of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy. Amendment cannot be allowed except for amending clerical errors such as changing the applicant for registration of extension and changing the patent number of the patent right eligible for registration of extension (see notes on wrongly-indicated patent numbers being correctable as clerical errors). Examiner shall determine legitimacy of subject for amendment; if amendment not eligible, deliver preliminary notice for inadmissible amendment and re-examine pre-amendment application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissible or improper amendments (co-owners and succession)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain amendments intended to correct applicant/co-owner issues or to change ownership are not recognized as legitimate amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If co-owners attempt to add an applicant who was not initially listed or change registered patent right holders to match applicants, such amendment shall not be recognized. Amendment of changing the patent applicant to a universal successor in presence of universal succession shall not be acknowledged. If amendment is inadmissible, examiner shall deliver notification for inadmissible amendment and examine the pre-amendment application again. A notification for inadmissible amendment can be included in a subsequent refusal notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in decision to register or to reject registration of extension
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a written decision to register extension or to reject an application for registration of extension, certain items shall be indicated in the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items to include: ① Number of application for registration of extension; ② Patent number; ③ Period for extension; ④ Content of approval or registration under Article 89 (claims for registration of extension, content of approval or registration, ground for extension, etc.); ⑤ Name and address of applicant for registration of extension (or entity title and business address); ⑥ Agent name/address or firm/title and designated attorney name; ⑦ Order of decision and ground for the decision; ⑧ Date of decision. (Items ③ and ④ need not be written in a written decision to reject.) Examiner must report intention to team leader and sign the written decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal and publication after decision to register extension
rubrics_metrics.description: When a decision to register patent term extension is made, specific transmittal and publication steps are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner shall deliver a copy of the decision to the applicant. Examiner shall ask registration division to include in the patent gazette: ① name and address of patent right holder (or entity title and business address), ② patent number, ③ date of registration of extension, ④ period for extension, ⑤ content of approval under Article 89 (indications such as claims for registration of extension, contents of approval or registration, ground for extension, etc.). See provisions regarding service of a copy of a decision to grant a patent for detailed transmittal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and invalidation procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who receive a written decision to reject registration of extension have recourse to appeal or invalidation trials under specified timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of appeal against a decision to reject registration of extension must be submitted within thirty days from date of receipt of the decision copy. If registration falls under Article 134(1) of the Patent Act, an applicant can request a trial to invalidate the registration of patent term extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of patent term for delays in registration (Article 92-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When registration of a patent right is delayed beyond statutory thresholds, the term of the patent may be extended by the delayed period, subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration delayed more than four years from filing date of patent application or three years from the date a request for examination is made (whichever later), the term may be extended as much as the delayed period, notwithstanding Article 88(1). Periods delayed due to an applicant shall be reduced from the extension period; where applicant-caused delay overlaps with registration delay, the reduction shall not exceed actual applicant-caused delay. Matters concerning 'period delayed due to an applicant' shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates to be deemed 'filing date' when calculating four-year threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating four years from the filing date for Article 92-2 purposes, specific alternative dates shall be deemed the filing date in certain cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dates include: 1) date when a legitimate right-holder applies (Article 34/35 cases); 2) date when a divisional application is filed (Article 52 cases); 3) date when a converted application is filed (Article 53 cases); 4) date when documents required for international application deemed as patent application submitted (Article 203(1)); 5) date when applicant requests KIPO decision for international application (Article 214(1)); 6) date when patent application is filed otherwise. Examiners should use these rules when computing the four-year threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'period delayed due to an applicant' (Enforcement Decree Article 7(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'period delayed due to an applicant' includes numerous specific procedural periods in which applicant actions or requests cause delay, spanning patent-office proceedings, litigation, and administrative appeal/litigation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Enforcement Decree enumerates detailed subcases, including (but not limited to): (1)(a)-(t) delays in patent-related proceedings before KIPO or the Trial and Appeal Board (e.g., time to appoint/replace agent, periods extended at applicant request, postponed dates at applicant request, suspensions/interruptions, applicant-requested consultations, specification amendments, claim withdrawal, delayed expedited examination determinations, applicant delays in submission of arguments, fee payments after grant steps, reexamination requests, requests for examination after a cause ceases, motions for disqualification not accepted, delayed evidence preservation conclusions, resumed reviews after closing, requests for retrials and related periods, service delays due to applicant); (2)(a)-(m) periods in litigation proceedings (e.g., stays, motions for disqualification of judges, court-ordered corrections, appointment of special representatives, resumed trials due to applicant, extensions/grants of additional periods, service delays); (3)(a)-(g) periods in administrative appeal or administrative litigation (e.g., rejections of disqualification requests, appeals after force majeure, Commission-ordered corrections, deadlines for supplemental briefs, postponed hearing dates, service provisions applied mutatis mutandis). Examiners must apply this comprehensive list to determine applicant-caused delay for deduction from extension.
